## **Copper Monthly October 2011 No. 178** #### **Highlights** ##### **INSIDE THIS ISSUE** ###### **China to face winter power shortages** Power shortages plagued many of China's provinces earlier this year and are likely to occur in China's southern and central regions this winter as demand for electricity increases, because of the rising coal prices. In addition, transportation costs are too high, which greatly increased power generation costs. The total of China's coal production and imports can meet the total consumption, but the transportation costs are too high, and speculators add more in the costs. Plant representatives and experts said coal traders buy one ton of coal for about 400 yuan in coal mines in Erdos, the Inner Mongolia autonomous region, which is a major coal producer in China, and the unit price will increase to as much as 900 yuan to 1,000 yuan when the coal is sold to power plants in Shanghai. Some companies cannot afford the coal prices because of the ongoing losses, and some others don't want large coal reserves because of the high prices ###### **_Highlights_** China to face winter power shortages...............1 ###### **_Copper Market Review_** Copper prices continue to slump………..……...2 Chinese refined copper imports hit third high in Aug………………………………….……............7 **_News_** World's biggest copper smelting anode furnace comes on stream at Tongling.….……..………..8 Fengshan Mine to over fulfill annual plan………….………..……..…………….……..9 High-precision copper foil project settles in Tianjin……………………….….………..…..….10 Jiangxi Copper produces ultrathin copper foill…….…………...……….…..…………..…....11 **Statistics** Chinese Refined Copper Output by Region in Aug 2011…………………….……. ……………14 Chinese Imports and Exports of Cu Products in Aug 2011………….…………..… …..…….....15 **_Market Data_** .…..… ..……….…..….…........23 China Electricity Council statistics show that all together, the power plants operated by the country's five major power generation groups-China Huaneng Group, China Datang Corp, China Guodian Corp, Website: www.antaike.com 1 Copper Monthly No. 178 China Huadian Corp and China Power Investment Corp - lost 7.46 bln yuan in the first seven months of this year, 8.27 bln yuan more than the same period in 2010. China needs to resolve coal transportation obstacles to help deliver coal from the north to the south and the west to the east. Otherwise, the high logistical costs will never be eased. A senior official from the National Energy Administration (NEA) warned that a prolonged drought in south China this summer that caused hydro electric power plant

s to generate less electricity. Hydroelectric power generation during the June-August period was down 39.1 percent year-on-year in east China, while power generated by the Three Gorges Dam, the world's largest hydroelectric power plant, was also down 16.9%. 

Hydropower-rich southwestern Chinese provinces and regions, including Guizhou, Guangxi and Yunnan, have been hit badly by droughts and poor hydro generation since early this year. Electricity supplies to many local industries as well as to the country's export hub of Guangdong have been reduced. XueJing, director of the statistics and information department under China Electricity Council (CEC) said a forecast production slowdown in the steel sector and in the nonferrous metals sectors and another round of an energy-saving drive could combine to limit demand growth in the fourth quarter. She did not provide any numerical estimate. 

#### **Copper Market Commentary** 

###### **Copper prices continue to slump** 

Copper for three month on LME opened at US$9,257/t on Sep.1, and closed at US$7,230/t on Sep.29, touching a high of US$9,257/t on Sep.1 and a low of US$7,230/t on Sep.29. 

The Federal Reserve announced "Operation Twist" on Sep 22, a widely expected stimulus move reviving a policy from the 1960s.The policy involves selling $400 bln in short-term Treasuries in exchange for the same amount of longer-term bonds, starting in October and ending in June 2012. It was just an expedient but far from a long-term and effective inspiriting mechanism. Moody's cuts BofA, Wells Fargo and Citigroup credit ratings increased tensions. Later, Group of 20 leaders pledged to take measures to prevent the European sovereign-debt crisis from worsening. Nevertheless, global economy was still in slumps. LME copper prices decreased by over 20% against that on Sep.1. 

Copper for three month on SHFE opened at 68,510 yuan/t on Sep.1, and closed at 52,600 yuan/t on Sep. 29, touching a high of 68,510 yuan/t on Sep.1 and a low of 52,600 yuan/t on Sep.29. 

Domestic copper prices followed the trend of copper prices on LME. Currently, with the coming of copper consumption in the off-season, together with financial pressures and consumption restriction in downstream enterprises, bargain buy to fill stocks is likely to be limited and turnover is expected to be low. In addition, copper inventory has a certain decline recently, from 107,790t on Sep.1 to 102.253t on Sep.23, which is favorable for market expectation, but only small driver due to the bigger uncertain

###### **Chinese refined copper output rises in August** 

Data released by China Nonferrous Metals Industry Association (CNIA) showed refined copper output was 499.35kt in August, up by 10.45% m-o-m or by 30.07% y-o-y. The accumulative output from January to August was 3.48Mt, up by 15.12% y-o-y. According to statistics from Antaike, during Jan to Aug, output of 12 Chinese main refined copper producers produced 2.56Mt, up by 13.80% y-o-y. Of them, growth rate of refined copper output in Bayin Nonferrous Metals Company, Shanghai Dachang Copper Co., Ltd, Jiangxi Copper Group, Dongying Fangyuan Nonferrous Metals Co., Daye Nonferrous Metals Co., Ltd. was 41.73%, 39.09%, 19.25%, 14.67% and 13.53% y-o-y respectively. Rising TC/RCs stimulated smelters’ production wish. TC/RCs in the long term contract market was around US$90/9 cents in the second half year of 2011, up 25% against US$72/7.2 cents in the first half year of 2011. Antaike estimates that domestic refined copper output will fall but still maintain at a relative high level in Sep, considering that copper price has been falling and copper concentrate import might not as high as it was in Aug. 

Copper semis output reached 935.35kt in Aug., up by 5% m-o-m. The m-o-m increase of copper semis output was mainly because major domestic copper-using products outputs had a m-o-m rise in Aug., such as power generating equipment, AC motor, electric wire and cables. But the coming of off-season consumption in air conditioning and refrigeration industry will inhibit consumption at a certain degree in future. 

Copper-in-concentrate output was 108.93kt in August, slightly by 1.23% m-o-m or up 9.23% y-o-y. The accumulative output from January to August was 808.03kt, up by 11.62% y-o-y. Analysis of data showed that copper-in-concentrate production of Jiangxi, Yunnan, Inner Mongolia, Anhui, xinjiang, etc.

###### **Copper consumption** 

According to the latest statistics from National Bureau of Statistics of China (NBS), major domestic copper-using products output in Jan-Aug increased year on year by two digits, except autos, AC motor, household ice-box, transformers and telecommunication cable. While, affected by off-season 

consumption in air conditioning and refrigeration industry, output of household refrigerator, household ice-box and a

ir conditioners had m-o-m declines in August. According to the statistics from China Electricity Council, total investment in electric power reached 393.9 bln yuan during January to August, up by 7.7% y-o-y. Of which investment in power source and power grid was 209.8 bln yuan and 184.1 bln yuan, up by 6.7% and 8.7 % y-o-y respectively. Of investment in power source, investment in hydropower and nuclear power increased by 34.9% and 30.1% y-o-y; investment in thermal power and wind power decreased by 10.3% and 13.7% y-o-y. The year-on-year decline of investment in wind power appeared since May 2011, which was mainly caused by the reduced investment in partial wind power provinces. At present, electric power industry is still the very import copper consumption sector. According to China Electricity Council statistics, the cumulative total power consumption in January and August was 3124.0 TWh, up by 11.89% y-o-y, 7.45 percentage points lower than the same period of 2010. Power consumption in August was 434.3 TWh, up by 9.09% y-o-y, 5.60 percentage points lower than the same period of 2010. While refined copper import decreased by 12% y-o-y in Aug.. During Jan to Aug, the cumulative refined copper import reached 1.51Mt, down by 26% y-o-y. It is difficult for refined copper import to continue to rise because of shrinking SHFE/LME arbitrage and falling copper prices, although copper consumption was still not bad in Chinese market. China’ refined copper export was less than 500t in Aug., down by 88% m-o-m. During Jan to Aug, the cumulative refined copper export reached 151.20kt, down by 639% y-o-y. Export decline of refined copper reflected that Chinese domestic copper consumption was still steady although copper off-season consumption was coming. As to copper concentrate, China’s copper concentrate import reached 675.24kt in Aug., up by 43% y-o-y and by about 50% m-o-m. During Jan to Aug, the cumulative copper concentrate import reached 4.07Mt, down by 5% y-o-y. Rise of domestic copper concentrate output can partially meet the gap caused by copper concentrate import. Statistics from China Customs still showed that copper scraps import was 382.18kt, down by 4% y-o-y and 12% m-o-m. During Jan. to Aug., the cumulative copper scraps import reached 301.14kt, up by 7% y-o-y.
